assignCourier(uint256,address).notice: VULNERABILITY 1: Access Control Vulnerability (OWASP SC01) ------------------------------------------------------------ This function is meant to be restricted to the logistics company (owner), but the onlyOwner modifier is intentionally left off. Any address can assign itself (or anyone else) as the courier for any shipment. Combined with updateStatus() below (which also lacks a "msg.sender == s.courier" check), an attacker can:   1. Call assignCourier(id, attackerAddress)   2. Call updateStatus(id, Status.Delivered)   3. Call releasePayment(id) to steal the escrowed fee      without ever delivering the parcel. Fix (do NOT apply yet - this is intentional for the assignment):   Add `onlyOwner` to assignCourier(), and require   `registeredCouriers[courier] == true`.

claimRefund(uint256).notice: VULNERABILITY 2: Reentrancy (OWASP SC05) ------------------------------------------------------------ The external call (sending ETH back to msg.sender) happens BEFORE the state is updated (s.refunded = true / fee = 0). A malicious contract calling this function can re-enter claimRefund() from its receive()/fallback() function and drain the escrowed fee multiple times, taking funds that belong to other shipments' senders and couriers. Fix (do NOT apply yet - this is intentional for the assignment):   Follow checks-effects-interactions: set s.refunded = true   and zero out s.fee BEFORE making the external call, or use   a reentrancy guard (nonReentrant modifier).

updateStatus(uint256,uint8).notice: Also part of VULNERABILITY 1 (OWASP SC01): This function should check `msg.sender == s.courier`, but that check is intentionally omitted so any address can move any shipment straight to Delivered. Fix (do NOT apply yet):   require(msg.sender == s.courier, "Not assigned courier");

VULNERABILITY 2: Reentrancy (OWASP SC05)
 ------------------------------------------------------------
 The external call (sending ETH back to msg.sender) happens
 BEFORE the state is updated (s.refunded = true / fee = 0).
 A malicious contract calling this function can re-enter
 claimRefund() from its receive()/fallback() function and
 drain the escrowed fee multiple times, taking funds that
 belong to other shipments' senders and couriers.
 Fix (do NOT apply yet - this is intentional for the assignment):
   Follow checks-effects-interactions: set s.refunded = true
   and zero out s.fee BEFORE making the external call, or use
   a reentrancy guard (nonReentrant modifier).

VULNERABILITY 1: Access Control Vulnerability (OWASP SC01)
 ------------------------------------------------------------
 This function is meant to be restricted to the logistics
 company (owner), but the onlyOwner modifier is intentionally
 left off. Any address can assign itself (or anyone else) as
 the courier for any shipment.
 Combined with updateStatus() below (which also lacks a
 "msg.sender == s.courier" check), an attacker can:
   1. Call assignCourier(id, attackerAddress)
   2. Call updateStatus(id, Status.Delivered)
   3. Call releasePayment(id) to steal the escrowed fee
      without ever delivering the parcel.
 Fix (do NOT apply yet - this is intentional for the assignment):
   Add `onlyOwner` to assignCourier(), and require
   `registeredCouriers[courier] == true`.

Also part of VULNERABILITY 1 (OWASP SC01):
 This function should check `msg.sender == s.courier`, but
 that check is intentionally omitted so any address can move
 any shipment straight to Delivered.
 Fix (do NOT apply yet):
   require(msg.sender == s.courier, "Not assigned courier");
